1.1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was chillin' with God, and the Word was God.
1.2: He was right there with God from the jump.
1.3: Everything that got made was made through Him. Not a single thing came to be without Him.
1.4: In Him was life, and that life was the light for all folks.
1.5: That light shined in the darkness, and the darkness ain't know what to do with it.
1.6: God sent a man named John.
1.7: John came as a witness, so he could speak on the Light, so folks would believe through him.
1.8: He wasn't the Light—he was just here to talk about the Light.
1.9: That Light he talked about? That was the real one, the one that gives light to everybody comin' into the world.
1.10: He was in the world, the world was made through Him, and the world ain't even recognize Him.
1.11: He pulled up to His own people, and they ain't want Him.
1.12: But the ones who did welcome Him—who believed in His name—He gave 'em the right to be God's children.
1.13: They ain't born from blood, or from fleshly desire, or some man's decision—but straight up from God.
1.14: The Word became human and moved into the neighborhood. We saw His glory—the kind only a Father's only Son got—full of grace and truth.
1.15: John talked about Him, shoutin', "This the One I told y'all about! The One who came after me, but ranks higher than me—'cause He existed before I did!"
1.16: From all He got, we all received—grace stacked on top of grace.
1.17: The law came through Moses, but grace and truth showed up through Jesus Christ.
1.18: Nobody ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who's right there close to the Father's heart—He made Him known.
1.19: This right here was John's testimony, when the Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who you?"
1.20: He straight up told 'em, "I ain't the Messiah."
1.21: They said, "Okay, so are you Elijah then?" He said, "Nah, not me." They said, "You the Prophet?" He said, "Nope."
1.22: Then they said, "Well who are you then? We gotta report back. What you sayin' about yourself?"
1.23: He said, "I'm just a voice shoutin' in the wilderness, sayin', 'Get the Lord's path straight,' just like Isaiah said."
1.24: The ones who came to him were from the Pharisees.
1.25: They asked, "So why you baptizin' if you not the Messiah, Elijah, or the Prophet?"
1.26: John said, "I baptize with water. But Somebody standin' right here among y'all, and y'all don't even know Him."
1.27: "He comin' after me, but He way greater. I ain't even worthy to untie His sandals."
1.28: All this went down in Bethany across the Jordan, where John was baptizin'.
1.29: The next day, John saw Jesus comin' and said, "Look! The Lamb of God, the One who takes away the world's sin!"
1.30: "This who I was talkin' about when I said, 'Somebody comin' after me who outranks me—'cause He was here before me.'"
1.31: "I ain't even know who He was at first. But I came baptizin' so He could be revealed to Israel."
1.32: John gave his testimony: "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove, and He stayed on Him."
1.33: "I ain't know who He was, but the One who sent me to baptize said, 'The one you see the Spirit land on and stay? That's Him—the One who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.'"
1.34: "I saw it for myself. That's the Son of God, no doubt."
1.35: The next day, John was standin' there with two of his disciples.
1.36: He looked at Jesus walkin' by and said, "Look—God's Lamb!"
1.37: When the two disciples heard him say that, they followed Jesus.
1.38: Jesus turned around and saw them followin'. He said, "What y'all want?" They said, "Rabbi"—which means Teacher—"where You stayin'?"
1.39: He said, "Come see for yourself." They went, saw where He was stayin', and chilled with Him that day. It was about 4pm.
1.40: One of the two that heard John and followed Jesus was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother.
1.41: First thing Andrew did was find his brother Simon and say, "We found the Messiah!"—which means the Christ.
1.42: Then he brought Simon to Jesus. Jesus looked him over and said, "You Simon, son of John? From now on, you go by Cephas"—which means Rock.
1.43: The next day, Jesus decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip and said, "Come roll with Me."
1.44: Philip was from Bethsaida, same town as Andrew and Peter.
1.45: Philip found Nathanael and told him, "We found the One Moses wrote about in the law—and the prophets too—Jesus of Nazareth, son of Joseph."
1.46: Nathanael said, "Nazareth? Ain't nothin' good come from there." Philip said, "Come see for yourself."
1.47: Jesus saw Nathanael comin' and said, "Now that's a real Israelite—ain't no cap in him!"
1.48: Nathanael asked, "How You know me?" Jesus said, "I saw you while you was sittin' under the fig tree, before Philip even called you."
1.49: Nathanael said, "Rabbi, You really are the Son of God. You the King of Israel!"
1.50: Jesus said, "You believe 'cause I said I saw you under that tree? You gon' see way more than that."
1.51: Then He said, "For real, I'm tellin' you—you gon' see heaven wide open, and angels goin' up and down on the Son of Man."

2.1: Three days later, there was a wedding in Cana over in Galilee. Jesus' mama was there too.
2.2: Jesus and His disciples got invited to the wedding as well.
2.3: When the wine ran out, Jesus' mama said to Him, "They outta wine."
2.4: Jesus said, "Ma'am, what that gotta do with Me? My time ain't come yet."
2.5: But His mama told the servants, "Whatever He tell y'all to do, just do it."
2.6: There was six big stone water jugs sittin' there—used for Jewish purification rituals. Each one held like twenty to thirty gallons.
2.7: Jesus said, "Fill up the waterpots with water." So they filled 'em all the way up to the top.
2.8: Then He told 'em, "Now scoop some out and take it to the master of the feast." So they did.
2.9: The master of the feast tasted the water that had turned into wine. He ain't know where it came from, but the servants did. The master called the groom over.
2.10: He said, "Man, usually folks bring out the good wine first, and then when folks good and tipsy, they bring out the cheap stuff. But you done saved the good wine for last!"
2.11: This was the first miracle Jesus did, right there in Cana of Galilee. It showed His glory, and His disciples started really believin' in Him.
2.12: After that, Jesus rolled down to Capernaum with His mama, His brothers, and His disciples. They ain't stay long.
2.13: The Jewish Passover was comin' up, so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
2.14: At the temple, He saw folks sellin' oxen, sheep, and doves, and He saw the money changers doin' business too.
2.15: Jesus made a whip outta cords, and started drivin' everybody out the temple—both people and animals. He flipped the money changers' tables and dumped all their coins out.
2.16: Then He told the dove sellers, "Get this stuff outta here! Don't turn My Father's house into a marketplace!"
2.17: His disciples remembered what the Scriptures said: "Zeal for Your house done ate Me up."
2.18: Then the Jewish leaders said, "What sign You gon' show us to prove You got authority to do all this?"
2.19: Jesus answered, "Tear down this temple, and I'll raise it back up in three days."
2.20: They said, "Man, it took forty-six years to build this temple. You think You can raise it in three days?"
2.21: But Jesus was talkin' about His body as the temple.
2.22: After He rose from the dead, His disciples remembered what He had said. That's when they fully believed the Scripture and His words.
2.23: While He was in Jerusalem for Passover, during the festival, a lotta folks believed in His name when they saw the miracles He was doin'.
2.24: But Jesus ain't put His trust in them, 'cause He knew what people was really about.
2.25: He ain't need nobody to tell Him what was inside folks—He already knew what was in their hearts.

3.1: Now check it out - there was this Pharisee named Nicodemus who was part of the Jewish leadership council.
3.2: This dude came to Jesus at night and said, 'Rabbi, we know you gotta be from God for real because ain't nobody could do these miraculous signs you doing unless God is with them.'
3.3: Jesus hit him back saying, 'Real talk, I'm telling you straight up - can't nobody see God's kingdom unless they get born again.'
3.4: Nicodemus was confused like, 'How somebody supposed to be born when they already old? You can't go back in your mama's womb and get born again!'
3.5: Jesus broke it down, 'Listen close now - ain't nobody getting into God's kingdom unless they born through water and the Spirit.'
3.6: What comes from human nature is human, but what comes from the Spirit is spirit.
3.7: Don't be shocked when I tell you that y'all gotta be born again.
3.8: The wind moves however it wants to. You hear it doing its thing, but you can't tell where it's coming from or where it's heading. That's exactly how it is with everybody born from the Spirit.
3.9: Nicodemus still wasn't getting it, asking, 'How all this supposed to work?'
3.10: Jesus was like, 'You supposed to be teaching Israel, and you don't even understand this?'
3.11: Real talk, we speaking on what we know and seen firsthand, but y'all still ain't trying to hear us.
3.12: If y'all don't believe when I'm talking bout earthly things, how you gonna believe when I start speaking on heavenly business?
3.13: Nobody ever made it to heaven except the One who came down from there - the Son of Man.
3.14: Just like Moses had to lift up that snake in the desert, that's how the Son of Man gotta be lifted up too,
3.15: so everybody who believes in Him can get that eternal life.
3.16: For real, God was showing mad love to the world when He gave up His one and only Son. Now anybody who believes in Him ain't gotta die but they getting eternal life instead.
3.17: See, God ain't send His Son to earth to condemn everybody. Nah, He sent Him to save the world through Him.
3.18: Whoever believes in Him ain't getting condemned. But if you ain't believing, you already condemned cause you ain't put your faith in God's one and only Son.
3.19: Here's the real situation: Light came through to the world, but people was feeling the darkness more than the light cause they was doing dirty.
3.20: Everybody out here doing wrong hates the light and won't come near it, cause they don't want their dirt exposed.
3.21: But people living in truth come to the light so everybody can see that what they doing is God's work.
3.22: After all this went down, Jesus and His crew headed out to the Judean countryside. He stayed there with them for a minute, baptizing folks.
3.23: John was doing his thing too, baptizing at Aenon near Salim cause there was plenty of water there, and people kept coming through to get baptized.
3.24: (This was before they locked John up.)
3.25: Some of John's disciples got into it with a Jewish dude about purification.
3.26: They came to John like, 'Rabbi, you know that dude who was with you on the other side of the Jordan? The one you was cosigning? Well, He out here baptizing now and everybody going to Him instead.'
3.27: John responded, 'Look, nobody can get nothing unless heaven gives it to them.'
3.28: Y'all can back me up on this - I been saying I ain't the Messiah. I'm just the one sent ahead to get things ready.
3.29: The bride belongs to the groom, feel me? The groom's homie just stands by, listening for him, getting hype when he hears the groom's voice. That's the kind of joy I got right now, and it's complete.
3.30: He gotta become more important while I become less important.
3.31: The One who comes from above is above everybody. Whoever's from earth belongs to earth and speaks earth talk. But the One from heaven is above all that.
3.32: He testifying bout what He seen and heard, but hardly nobody trying to accept His testimony.
3.33: Whoever does accept His testimony is cosigning that God is truthful.
3.34: The One God sent speaks God's words, cause God ain't holding back the Spirit when it comes to Him.
3.35: The Father loves the Son and put everything in His hands.
3.36: Whoever believes in the Son got eternal life right now, but whoever ain't trying to hear the Son ain't gonna see life - they just gonna keep catching God's wrath.

4.1: When the Lord heard the Pharisees was talkin' about how Jesus was makin' and baptizin' more disciples than John,
4.2: (even though Jesus Himself wasn't baptizin', His disciples were),
4.3: He left Judea and went back up to Galilee.
4.4: But He had to go through Samaria to get there.
4.5: He pulled up to a town in Samaria called Sychar, close to the land Jacob gave his son Joseph.
4.6: Jacob's well was there, and Jesus, tired from the trip, sat down by the well. It was about noon.
4.7: A Samaritan woman came to get some water. Jesus said, "Can you get Me a drink?"
4.8: His disciples had gone into town to grab some food.
4.9: The Samaritan woman said, "Hold up—you a Jew, and I'm a Samaritan woman. Why you askin' me for a drink?" (Jews ain't mess with Samaritans like that.)
4.10: Jesus said, "If you knew the gift God got for you, and who I am, you'd be askin' Me for water—and I'd give you livin' water."
4.11: She said, "Sir, You ain't got nothin' to draw with, and this well deep. Where You gon' get that livin' water?
4.12: You think You greater than Jacob, our ancestor, who gave us this well? He drank from it, so did his sons and his animals."
4.13: Jesus said, "Anybody who drinks this water gon' be thirsty again.
4.14: But whoever drinks the water I give won't ever be thirsty again. That water gon' turn into a spring inside them—overflowin' with eternal life."
4.15: The woman said, "Sir, give me that water then! So I won't be thirsty or have to come back here."
4.16: Jesus said, "Go get your man and come back."
4.17: She said, "I don't got no man." Jesus said, "You right when you say that.
4.18: You done had five men, and the one you got now ain't your husband. So yeah, you told the truth."
4.19: She said, "Sir… I see You a prophet.
4.20: Our people worshipped on this mountain, but y'all Jews say we gotta worship in Jerusalem."
4.21: Jesus said, "Woman, believe Me—time's comin' when it won't matter if you worship on this mountain or in Jerusalem.
4.22: Y'all worship what you don't know. We worship what we know, 'cause salvation comes through the Jews.
4.23: But the time comin'—matter fact, it's here now—when real worshippers gon' worship the Father in spirit and in truth. That's the kind the Father lookin' for.
4.24: God is Spirit, so if you gon' worship Him, it gotta be in spirit and truth."
4.25: She said, "I know the Messiah's comin'—He's called the Christ. When He gets here, He gon' break it all down."
4.26: Jesus said, "That's Me. The one you talkin' to."
4.27: Just then, His disciples came back. They was shocked He was talkin' to a woman, but nobody asked, "What You want?" or "Why You talkin' to her?"
4.28: She left her water jar and ran back to the city. She told the people,
4.29: "Come see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could He be the Christ?"
4.30: They left the city and went lookin' for Him.
4.31: Meanwhile, His disciples was sayin', "Rabbi, You need to eat something."
4.32: Jesus said, "I got food y'all don't know nothin' about."
4.33: The disciples looked at each other like, "Who brought Him food?"
4.34: Jesus said, "My food is doin' the will of the One who sent Me, and finishin' His work.
4.35: Y'all always say, 'Four more months till harvest,' but I'm tellin' y'all—look around. The fields already ripe.
4.36: The one who harvests gets paid and gathers fruit that lasts forever. So the sower and the reaper both get to celebrate.
4.37: The sayin' true: one person plants, another one harvests.
4.38: I sent y'all to harvest fields y'all ain't work for. Other folks did the grindin', and y'all just steppin' into the blessing."
4.39: A lotta Samaritans from that town believed in Him just off what the woman said: "He told me everything I ever did."
4.40: When the Samaritans came to Him, they begged Him to stay. So He stayed two more days.
4.41: And way more folks believed—this time off Jesus' own words.
4.42: They told the woman, "We believe now not just 'cause of what you said, but 'cause we heard Him ourselves. Now we know He's the Christ, the Savior of the world."
4.43: After them two days, Jesus left and went back to Galilee.
4.44: Jesus had already said, "A prophet don't get no love in his own hometown."
4.45: But when He got to Galilee, the people welcomed Him, 'cause they saw everything He did in Jerusalem during the festival—they was there too.
4.46: He went back to Cana in Galilee, where He turned water into wine. There was this official whose son was sick back in Capernaum.
4.47: When he heard Jesus was back from Judea, he went to Him and begged Him to come heal his son, who was about to die.
4.48: Jesus said, "Y'all won't believe unless you see signs and miracles, huh?"
4.49: The man said, "Sir, please come before my child dies!"
4.50: Jesus told him, "Go on home—your son's alive." The man believed what Jesus said and headed back.
4.51: While he was on his way, his servants met him and said, "Your son is alive!"
4.52: He asked what time the boy got better. They said, "Yesterday, around one in the afternoon, the fever broke."
4.53: The father realized that's the exact time Jesus had said, "Your son lives." And he believed—him and his whole household.
4.54: This was the second miracle Jesus did after comin' back from Judea into Galilee.

5.1: After that, there was a Jewish feast, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
5.2: In Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, there's a pool called Bethesda in Hebrew. It got five porches.
5.3: A whole crowd of sick folks would lay there—blind, lame, and paralyzed—waitin' on the water to move.
5.4: 'Cause at certain times, an angel would come stir up the water. First one in after that? Got healed from whatever they had.
5.5: One man had been sick for thirty-eight years.
5.6: When Jesus saw him layin' there and knew he been in that shape for a long time, He asked, "You tryna get well or nah?"
5.7: The man said, "Sir, I ain't got nobody to help me into the pool when the water gets stirred. Every time I try, somebody beats me to it."
5.8: Jesus told him, "Get up. Pick up your mat and walk."
5.9: Right then, the man got healed. He picked up his mat and started walkin'. And it just so happened that was on the Sabbath day.
5.10: The Jewish leaders told the man who got healed, "Hey, it's the Sabbath. You ain't supposed to be carryin' that mat."
5.11: He said, "The man who healed me is the one who told me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"
5.13: But the healed man ain't know who it was—Jesus had dipped into the crowd right after.
5.14: Later on, Jesus found him in the temple and said, "Look at you—healed and all. Don't go back to sin, or something worse might come on you."
5.15: The man left and told the Jewish leaders it was Jesus who healed him.
5.16: That's why the Jews started goin' after Jesus and tryna kill Him—'cause He did this on the Sabbath.
5.17: Jesus told 'em, "My Father been workin' non-stop, and I'm workin' too."
5.18: That made 'em even madder. Not only was He breakin' Sabbath rules—they said He was makin' Himself equal with God by callin' God His Father.
5.19: Jesus said, "For real, for real—I'm tellin' y'all—the Son don't do nothin' on His own. He only do what He sees the Father do. Whatever the Father does, the Son do too.
5.20: The Father loves the Son and shows Him everything. And He gon' show even bigger things—just wait, y'all gon' be shook.
5.21: Just like the Father raises the dead and gives 'em life, the Son gives life to whoever He wants.
5.22: The Father ain't judging nobody—He gave that whole job to the Son.
5.23: So everybody gotta honor the Son just like they honor the Father. If you ain't honoring the Son, you ain't honoring the Father who sent Him.
5.24: Listen up—I'm tellin' you the truth: if you hear what I'm sayin' and believe the One who sent Me, you got eternal life. You ain't gotta worry about judgment—you already crossed from death to life.
5.25: Truth is, the time's comin'—matter fact, it's already here—when the dead gon' hear the voice of God's Son, and the ones who listen? Gon' live.
5.26: Just like the Father got life in Himself, He gave the Son that same kinda life.
5.27: And He gave the Son authority to judge too—'cause He the Son of Man.
5.28: Don't get it twisted—time's comin' when everybody in the grave gon' hear His voice,
5.29: and they gon' come out—those who did good things gon' rise up to eternal life, and the ones who did wrong? Gon' rise up to face judgment.
5.30: I don't do nothin' on My own. I judge based on what I hear. And My judgment right—'cause I ain't here to do what I want, but what the One who sent Me wants.
5.31: If I was out here speakin' on My own behalf, y'all wouldn't need to listen.
5.32: But there's Somebody else who speaks for Me, and I know He tellin' the truth.
5.33: Y'all sent folks to John, and he told y'all straight-up truth.
5.34: I don't need no man's validation—but I said all that so y'all might get saved.
5.35: John was like a lit-up lamp, burnin' bright, and for a little while, y'all liked that glow.
5.36: But I got somethin' better than John's testimony—the works the Father gave Me to do. The miracles I'm doin'? They prove the Father sent Me.
5.37: And the Father Himself, who sent Me, already testified 'bout Me. But y'all never heard His voice or seen Him.
5.38: His word don't even live in y'all, 'cause you ain't believe the One He sent.
5.39: Y'all stay searchin' the Scriptures thinkin' they the key to eternal life. But they really talkin' 'bout Me.
5.40: And still—you won't come to Me to get that life.
5.41: I don't need no clout from people.
5.42: But I know y'all—y'all ain't got the love of God in you.
5.43: I came in My Father's name and y'all ain't accept Me. But let somebody else come in they own name? Y'all quick to receive them.
5.44: How you gon' believe when you chasin' praise from each other but ain't seekin' the honor that come from God alone?
5.45: Don't think I'ma be the one to snitch on y'all to the Father. Moses—the one y'all swear by? He already speakin' against y'all.
5.46: If y'all really believed Moses, you'd believe Me—'cause he was talkin' about Me.
5.47: But since y'all don't even believe what he wrote, how you gon' believe what I'm sayin'?

6.1: After all that, Jesus crossed over the Sea of Galilee—also called the Sea of Tiberias.
6.2: A big crowd followed Him 'cause they seen the signs He did when He healed the sick.
6.3: Jesus went up on a mountain and sat down with His disciples.
6.4: The Jewish Passover was gettin' close.
6.5: Jesus looked up, saw a big crowd comin' toward Him, and said to Philip, "Where we gon' buy bread to feed all these folks?"
6.6: He said that to test Philip, 'cause Jesus already knew what He was gon' do.
6.7: Philip said, "Man, even 200 days' worth of money wouldn't be enough to give everybody even a lil piece."
6.8: Then Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, said,
6.9: "There's a boy here with five barley loaves and two small fish—but that ain't nearly enough for all these people."
6.10: Jesus said, "Tell everybody to sit down." There was a lotta grass there, so they sat down—about five thousand men.
6.11: Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and passed 'em to the disciples to hand out. Same with the fish—folks ate as much as they wanted.
6.12: When everybody was full, Jesus told His disciples, "Gather up all the leftovers so none of it gets wasted."
6.13: They picked up twelve baskets full of scraps from the five loaves—just from what was left after folks ate.
6.14: When the people saw the miracle Jesus had done, they said, "This gotta be the Prophet we been waitin' for!"
6.15: But when Jesus realized they was about to come snatch Him up and force Him to be king, He slipped away to the mountain by Himself.
6.16: That evenin', His disciples went down to the sea,
6.17: Got in a boat and started headin' toward Capernaum. It was dark, and Jesus hadn't come back yet.
6.18: A strong wind came through and stirred the water up.
6.19: After they rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus walkin' on the water, comin' toward the boat—and they got scared.
6.20: But Jesus said, "It's Me. Don't be scared."
6.21: They let Him in the boat, and right then—they hit land, exactly where they was headin'.
6.22: The next day, the crowd that had stayed on the other side of the sea realized there was only one boat, and that Jesus didn't leave in it—His disciples did.
6.23: More boats came in from Tiberias, near where they had eaten the bread after Jesus gave thanks.
6.24: When the crowd saw Jesus and His disciples weren't there, they got in the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.
6.25: When they found Him across the sea, they said, "Rabbi, when You get over here?"
6.26: Jesus said, "Truth is, y'all lookin' for Me not 'cause you saw signs, but 'cause you got full off that bread."
6.27: "Don't work for food that spoils—work for the food that gives eternal life. That's what the Son of Man gon' give you. God the Father already stamped Him with approval."
6.28: They said, "What we gotta do to do God's work?"
6.29: Jesus said, "Here's God's work: believe in the One He sent."
6.30: Then they asked, "What sign You gon' do so we can believe You? What You gon' show us?
6.31: Our ancestors ate manna in the desert, like Scripture says: 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
6.32: Jesus said, "Listen close—Moses ain't give y'all that bread from heaven. My Father gives the real bread from heaven."
6.33: "The bread God gives is the One who comes down from heaven and gives life to the whole world."
6.34: They said, "Lord, give us that bread every day."
6.35: Jesus said, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me won't ever go hungry. Whoever believes in Me won't ever be thirsty."
6.36: But I already told y'all—y'all seen Me and still don't believe.
6.37: Everybody the Father gives Me gon' come to Me. And anybody that comes to Me? I'll never turn 'em away.
6.38: I ain't come down from heaven to do what I want—I came to do what the One who sent Me wants.
6.39: And this is His will: that I don't lose none of the ones He gave Me, but raise 'em back up on the last day.
6.40: His will is that anybody who sees the Son and believes in Him gets eternal life. I'll raise 'em up on the last day too.
6.41: Then the Jews started complainin' 'cause He said, "I'm the bread that came down from heaven."
6.42: They was like, "Ain't this Jesus, Joseph's boy? We know His mom and dad. How He gon' say He came down from heaven?"
6.43: Jesus said, "Y'all need to stop murmurin' amongst yourselves.
6.44: Nobody can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws 'em. And I'll raise that one up on the last day.
6.45: The prophets wrote, 'They gon' all be taught by God.' So whoever listens and learns from the Father comes to Me.
6.46: Nobody's seen the Father except the One who came from God. He the only One that seen Him.
6.47: Real talk—anybody who believes in Me already got eternal life.
6.48: I am the bread of life.
6.49: Y'all ancestors ate manna in the wilderness… and they still died.
6.50: But this bread right here come from heaven—and whoever eats it won't die.
6.51: I'm the livin' bread that came down from heaven. If you eat this bread, you gon' live forever. And the bread I'm givin' is My flesh—for the life of the world."
6.52: The Jews started arguin' with each other like, "How He expect us to eat His flesh?"
6.53: Jesus said, "Listen up—unless y'all eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, y'all don't have no life in you.
6.54: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood got eternal life. And I'll raise 'em up on the last day.
6.55: 'Cause My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.
6.56: If you eat My flesh and drink My blood, you stay in Me, and I stay in you.
6.57: Just like the livin' Father sent Me, and I live 'cause of Him, the one who feeds on Me gon' live 'cause of Me.
6.58: This the bread that came down from heaven. It ain't like the manna y'all ancestors ate—'cause they died. But whoever eats this bread gon' live forever."
6.59: He said all this while teachin' in the synagogue in Capernaum.
6.60: When a lotta His disciples heard this, they said, "This is a hard word. Who can even take this in?"
6.61: Jesus already knew in His spirit that they was grumblin', so He said, "This trippin' y'all up?
6.62: What if y'all saw the Son of Man go back up to where He came from?
6.63: The Spirit is what gives life—the flesh don't do nothin'. The words I'm speakin'? They full of Spirit and life.
6.64: But some of y'all still don't believe." (Jesus already knew from the jump who didn't believe and who was gon' betray Him.)
6.65: And He said, "That's why I told y'all—can't nobody come to Me unless the Father gives 'em the green light."
6.66: From then on, a lotta His disciples dipped and didn't walk with Him no more.
6.67: So Jesus turned to the twelve and said, "Y'all wanna bounce too?"
6.68: Simon Peter said, "Lord, where else we gon' go? You got the words of eternal life.
6.69: We believe You, and we know You the Christ, the Son of the livin' God."
6.70: Jesus said, "Didn't I choose all twelve of y'all? But one of y'all is a devil."
6.71: He was talkin' about Judas Iscariot, Simon's son—'cause he was the one who was gon' betray Him, even though he was one of the twelve.

7.1: After that, Jesus was walkin' around Galilee. He wasn't tryna go to Judea 'cause the Jewish leaders was out to kill Him.
7.2: The Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was comin' up.
7.3: So His brothers said, "Man, leave here and go to Judea so Your disciples can see what You doin'.
7.4: Ain't nobody tryna be famous doin' stuff in secret. If You really bout it, show Yourself to the world."
7.5: Even His own brothers ain't believe in Him.
7.6: Jesus said, "My time ain't come yet, but y'all can move whenever. Your time always on go.
7.7: The world don't hate y'all, but it hates Me 'cause I tell the truth about how wicked it is.
7.8: Y'all go ahead to the feast. I ain't goin' just yet—My time ain't fully here."
7.9: After He told 'em that, He stayed back in Galilee.
7.10: But after His brothers left for the feast, He slid up there too—but on the low, not tryna be seen.
7.11: The Jewish leaders was lookin' for Him at the feast like, "Where He at?"
7.12: The crowd was whisperin' all kinds of stuff. Some said, "He a good man." Others said, "Nah, He foolin' people."
7.13: But nobody was sayin' it loud—'cause they was scared of the leaders.
7.14: Halfway through the feast, Jesus showed up at the temple and started teachin'.
7.15: The Jews was shook like, "How He know so much if He ain't never been to school?"
7.16: Jesus said, "What I'm teachin' ain't from Me—it's from the One who sent Me.
7.17: If you really tryin' to do God's will, you'll know whether My words come from Him or if I'm just talkin' for Me.
7.18: Folks who speak for themselves lookin' for their own shine. But the one who speaks for the One who sent Him? That one's real, and he ain't got no lies in him.
7.19: Ain't Moses give y'all the law? But none of y'all even keep it. So why y'all tryna kill Me?"
7.20: The crowd said, "You got a demon. Who tryna kill You?"
7.21: Jesus said, "I did one miracle, and now y'all actin' brand new.
7.22: Y'all circumcise on the Sabbath—Moses gave y'all that tradition (really came from the ancestors though).
7.23: So if y'all can circumcise on the Sabbath and not trip, why you mad that I healed a whole man on the Sabbath?
7.24: Stop judgin' by how stuff looks. Judge with righteous judgment."
7.25: Some folks from Jerusalem said, "Ain't this the dude they been tryna kill?
7.26: But look—He talkin' bold, and nobody sayin' nothin'. Maybe the leaders know He really the Christ?"
7.27: "But wait—we know where He from. When the Christ shows up, ain't nobody supposed to know His origins."
7.28: Jesus cried out in the temple, sayin', "Y'all know Me? Know where I'm from? I ain't come here on My own—God sent Me. And y'all don't even know Him.
7.29: But I do. I came from Him. He's the One who sent Me."
7.30: They tried to grab Him then, but nobody laid hands on Him—His time hadn't come yet.
7.31: A lotta folks in the crowd believed in Him. They said, "When the Christ comes, is He gon' do more miracles than this man?"
7.32: The Pharisees heard the crowd murmurin' like that, so the chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to arrest Him.
7.33: Jesus said, "I'm only gon' be here a lil while longer, then I'm goin' back to the One who sent Me.
7.34: Y'all gon' look for Me, but you ain't gon' find Me. Where I'm goin', you can't come."
7.35: The Jews was like, "Where He talkin' bout goin'? To the scattered Jews in other countries? He gon' teach the Greeks?"
7.36: "What He mean, 'You gon' look for Me and not find Me,' and 'Where I'm at, you can't come'?"
7.37: On the last and biggest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and yelled, "If anybody thirsty, come to Me and drink.
7.38: If you believe in Me, just like the Scriptures say, rivers of livin' water gon' flow outta your heart."
7.39: He was talkin' about the Spirit, which folks who believed in Him would receive. The Holy Spirit hadn't come yet 'cause Jesus hadn't been glorified yet.
7.40: Some folks in the crowd said, "For real, this Man is the Prophet."
7.41: Others said, "This is the Christ!" But some were like, "Hold up—Christ ain't supposed to come from Galilee.
7.42: Don't the Scriptures say He's supposed to come from David's family? From Bethlehem, where David was born?"
7.43: So folks was divided 'cause of Him.
7.44: Some wanted to arrest Him, but nobody laid a hand on Him.
7.45: The officers went back to the chief priests and Pharisees, and they said, "Why ain't y'all bring Him?"
7.46: They said, "Man, nobody ever talked like Him before."
7.48: Ain't none of the rulers or Pharisees believed in Him.
7.49: This crowd don't even know the law—they cursed."
7.50: Nicodemus (the one who came to Jesus at night, and was one of them) spoke up:
7.51: "Our law don't judge a man without hearin' him out and findin' out what he did—right?"
7.52: They said, "You from Galilee too? Search the Scriptures—ain't no prophet ever came from Galilee."
7.53: Then everybody went back to they own house.

8.1: Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
8.2: Early the next morning, He came back to the temple. All the people showed up, and He sat down to teach.
8.3: The scribes and Pharisees brought a woman who had got caught in adultery. They made her stand right there in front of everybody.
8.4: They said, "Teacher, this woman got caught in the act—in the act—of adultery.
8.5: Moses' law say we supposed to stone women like this. What You say?"
8.6: They was tryna trap Him—lookin' for somethin' to use against Him. But Jesus bent down and started writin' in the dirt like He didn't even hear 'em.
8.7: They kept pressin' Him, so He stood up and said, "Whoever ain't never sinned—go ahead, throw the first stone."
8.8: Then He bent back down and kept writin' on the ground.
8.9: One by one, they walked away—startin' with the older folks—'cause their conscience started checkin' 'em. Soon it was just Jesus and the woman standin' there.
8.10: Jesus stood up and asked her, "Where they at? Ain't nobody stick around to condemn you?"
8.11: She said, "No one, Lord." Jesus said, "Well I don't condemn you either. Go on now—and don't sin no more."
8.12: Then Jesus spoke again: "I'm the light of the world. If you follow Me, you won't walk in darkness—you'll have the light that gives life."
8.13: The Pharisees said, "You talkin' about Yourself—so Your testimony ain't valid."
8.14: Jesus said, "Even if I am speakin' on My own, it's still true—'cause I know where I came from and where I'm goin'. Y'all don't know either."
8.15: "Y'all judge by outward appearances. I don't judge anybody.
8.16: But even if I did, My judgment would still be right—'cause I ain't judging alone. The Father who sent Me is with Me."
8.17: "Y'all law says two witnesses make it valid.
8.18: Well, I testify about Myself—and My Father who sent Me does too."
8.19: They asked, "Where your Father at?" Jesus said, "Y'all don't know Me or My Father. If you knew Me, you'd know Him too."
8.20: Jesus said all this while teachin' in the treasury area of the temple. But nobody laid hands on Him, 'cause His time hadn't come yet.
8.21: Then Jesus said, "I'm goin' away. Y'all gon' look for Me, but you gon' die in your sins. Where I'm goin', y'all can't come."
8.22: The Jews said, "What He mean—He gon' kill Himself? Talkin' bout, 'Y'all can't come where I'm goin'?"
8.23: Jesus said, "Y'all from below. I'm from above. Y'all belong to this world—I don't.
8.24: That's why I said you gon' die in your sins. If you don't believe I am who I say I am, you will die in your sins."
8.25: They said, "Who are You?" Jesus said, "I been tellin' y'all from the jump.
8.26: I got a lot to say about y'all, and I could judge you right now. But the One who sent Me is real, and I only speak what I heard from Him."
8.27: But they still ain't realize He was talkin' about the Father.
8.28: So Jesus said, "When y'all lift up the Son of Man, then you gon' know I am who I say I am. I don't do nothin' on My own—I speak what the Father taught Me.
8.29: And the One who sent Me is with Me. He ain't left Me out here by Myself—'cause I always do what pleases Him."
8.30: While He was sayin' all that, many people started believin' in Him.
8.31: Jesus said to the Jews who believed Him, "If y'all stick with My word, you really My disciples.
8.32: And you'll know the truth—and the truth gon' set you free."
8.33: They said, "We Abraham's kids. We ain't never been slaves. How you gon' say we'll be made free?"
8.34: Jesus said, "Truth is—whoever sins is a slave to sin.
8.35: And slaves don't stay in the house forever, but the Son do.
8.36: So if the Son sets you free—you really free."
8.37: "I know y'all Abraham's descendants—but you tryna kill Me 'cause My word ain't got no place in you.
8.38: I'm speakin' on what I seen with My Father. But y'all do what you seen with your father."
8.39: They said, "Abraham is our father." Jesus said, "If y'all was really Abraham's kids, you'd act like him.
8.40: But instead you tryin' to kill Me—a man who told you the truth from God. Abraham didn't act like that.
8.41: Y'all doin' what your real father does." They said, "We ain't illegitimate. We got one Father—God."
8.42: Jesus said, "If God was really your Father, you'd love Me—'cause I came from Him. I didn't come on My own—He sent Me.
8.43: Why y'all don't get what I'm sayin'? 'Cause you don't wanna hear it.
8.44: You from your father—the devil. And you wanna do what he does. He been a murderer from the start. He don't stand in truth 'cause there ain't no truth in him. When he lies, he speakin' his native language—he the father of lies.
8.45: But since I'm tellin' the truth, y'all don't believe Me.
8.46: Which one of y'all can prove I sinned? So if I'm speakin' the truth, why won't y'all believe Me?
8.47: The ones who belong to God listen to God's words. That's why y'all don't hear Me—'cause you ain't from God."
8.48: Then the Jews said, "See? We told y'all He a Samaritan with a demon!"
8.49: Jesus said, "I ain't got no demon. I honor My Father—and y'all dishonorin' Me.
8.50: I ain't out here chasin' fame. There's One who handles that—and He judges.
8.51: I'm tellin' y'all the truth—anybody who keeps My word will never see death."
8.52: They said, "Now we know You got a demon! Abraham and the prophets died—but You say whoever follows You won't die?
8.53: You think You greater than Abraham who's dead? And the prophets? Who do You think You are?"
8.54: Jesus said, "If I hype Myself up, it don't mean nothin'. My Father—the One y'all call your God—He the One who gives Me glory.
8.55: But y'all don't even know Him. I know Him. And if I said I didn't, I'd be lyin' like y'all. But I do know Him, and I follow His word.
8.56: Your father Abraham was hyped to see My day. He saw it and got glad."
8.57: They said, "You ain't even fifty years old. How you seen Abraham?"
8.58: Jesus said, "Let Me be real with you—before Abraham was ever born… I AM."
8.59: Then they picked up stones to throw at Him—but Jesus dipped out the temple, slid through the crowd, and bounced.

9.1: As Jesus was passin' by, He saw a man who'd been blind since birth.
9.2: His disciples asked, "Rabbi, who messed up? This man or his parents, that he was born blind?"
9.3: Jesus said, "Ain't nobody sinned—it happened so God's power could be seen through him."
9.4: "We gotta do what the One who sent Me called us to do while it's still daytime. Night's comin' when nobody can work.
9.5: As long as I'm here in the world, I am the light of the world."
9.6: After sayin' that, Jesus spit on the ground, made some mud with it, and rubbed it on the man's eyes.
9.7: Then He told him, "Go wash in the pool of Siloam" (which means "Sent"). The man went, washed up, and came back able to see.
9.8: His neighbors and the folks who used to see him beggin' said, "Hold up—isn't that the same dude who used to sit and beg?"
9.9: Some said, "That's him!" Others said, "Nah, he just look like him." But he said, "It's me. I'm him."
9.10: So they asked, "Then how your eyes get opened?"
9.11: He said, "This dude named Jesus made some clay, rubbed it on my eyes, told me to go to Siloam and wash. I did—and now I can see."
9.12: They said, "Where He at?" He said, "I don't know."
9.13: They took the man who used to be blind to the Pharisees.
9.14: Now, Jesus did this on a Sabbath—yep, the day of rest.
9.15: So the Pharisees asked him again how it happened. He said, "He put clay on my eyes, I washed, and now I see."
9.16: Some of the Pharisees said, "He can't be from God—He breakin' Sabbath rules." But others said, "How can a sinner do miracles like this?" So now they was split.
9.17: They turned back to the man and said, "Well, what you think about Him since He opened your eyes?" He said, "He a prophet."
9.18: But the Jewish leaders ain't believe he had really been blind until they called his parents in.
9.19: They asked them, "Is this your son? The one y'all say was born blind? How he seein' now?"
9.20: His parents said, "Yeah, that's our son, and he was born blind.
9.21: But how he's seein' now—or who made it happen—we don't know. He grown. Ask him."
9.22: They said all that 'cause they was scared. The Jewish leaders had already decided anybody who said Jesus was the Christ was gon' get kicked out the synagogue.
9.23: That's why they said, "He grown—ask him."
9.24: So they went back to the man and said, "Tell the truth and give God the glory. We know that man Jesus is a sinner."
9.25: He said, "Look, I don't know if He a sinner or not. What I do know is: I was blind, and now I see."
9.26: They said, "What did He do to you? How exactly did He open your eyes?"
9.27: He said, "I already told y'all, and you ain't listen. Why you wanna hear it again? Y'all tryna become His disciples too?"
9.28: Then they started talkin' slick and said, "You His disciple—we follow Moses.
9.29: We know God talked to Moses. But this dude? We don't even know where He came from."
9.30: The man said, "That's wild. Y'all don't know where He from, but He opened my eyes.
9.31: We all know God don't hear from folks livin' in sin—but He does hear folks who worship Him and follow His will.
9.32: Ain't nobody in history ever opened the eyes of somebody born blind.
9.33: If He wasn't from God, He couldn't do nothin'."
9.34: They said, "You was born in sin from the jump, and you tryna school us?" Then they threw him out.
9.35: Jesus heard they had kicked him out. When He found him, He asked, "Do you believe in the Son of God?"
9.36: The man said, "Who is He, Lord? I'll believe if You tell me."
9.37: Jesus said, "You lookin' at Him—and He the one talkin' to you."
9.38: The man said, "Lord, I believe!" And he started worshipin' Him.
9.39: Then Jesus said, "I came into this world to bring judgment—so the blind can see, and the ones who think they see get exposed as blind."
9.40: Some Pharisees nearby heard that and said, "Wait—You sayin' we blind too?"
9.41: Jesus said, "If y'all was really blind, you wouldn't be guilty. But since you claim you can see—your guilt still stand."

10.1: "For real, for real—I'm tellin' y'all: anybody who don't come in through the sheep gate, but try to climb in some other way? That person a thief and a robber.
10.2: But the one who enters through the gate? That's the real shepherd.
10.3: The gatekeeper opens the door for him, and the sheep know his voice. He calls 'em by name and leads 'em out.
10.4: After he brings 'em out, he walks in front of 'em, and they follow—'cause they know his voice.
10.5: They won't follow a stranger though. Nah, they'll run the other way 'cause they don't recognize that voice."
10.6: Jesus used this lil parable, but they ain't understand what He was tryna say.
10.7: So Jesus broke it down again: "For real, for real—I'm the gate for the sheep.
10.8: All the folks that came before Me? Thieves and robbers. But My sheep ain't listen to 'em.
10.9: I'm the gate. Anybody who enters through Me gets saved. They'll come in, go out, and find green pastures.
10.10: The thief only come to steal, kill, and destroy. But I came so they can have life—real life, full and abundant.
10.11: I'm the Good Shepherd. And the Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
10.12: But the hired hand? He ain't the shepherd, and the sheep ain't his. So when he sees a wolf comin', he dip out and leaves the sheep. Then the wolf snatches 'em and scatters 'em.
10.13: The hired hand runs 'cause he only in it for the check. He don't really care about the sheep.
10.14: I'm the Good Shepherd. I know My sheep—and My sheep know Me,
10.15: Just like the Father knows Me and I know Him. And I lay down My life for My sheep.
10.16: I got other sheep that ain't from this pen. I gotta bring them too. They gon' hear My voice, and we gon' be one flock under one Shepherd.
10.17: That's why My Father loves Me—'cause I lay My life down so I can take it back again.
10.18: Nobody takin' it from Me—I lay it down on My own. I got the power to lay it down, and I got the power to pick it back up. That's the assignment I got from My Father."
10.19: When He said all that, the Jews started arguin' again.
10.20: Some said, "He got a demon—He crazy! Why y'all listenin' to Him?"
10.21: Others said, "This ain't how somebody with a demon talks. Can a demon make blind folks see?"
10.22: It was the Festival of Dedication in Jerusalem, and it was winter.
10.23: Jesus was walkin' through the temple, over in Solomon's porch.
10.24: The Jews crowded around Him and said, "How long You gon' keep us guessin'? If You the Christ, just say it straight."
10.25: Jesus said, "I already told y'all, and you ain't believe Me. The works I do in My Father's name—they speak for Me.
10.26: But y'all don't believe 'cause you ain't My sheep.
10.27: My sheep know My voice. I know 'em, and they follow Me.
10.28: I give 'em eternal life—they ain't never gon' perish. Nobody can snatch 'em out My hand.
10.29: My Father gave 'em to Me, and He's greater than everybody. Can't nobody snatch 'em out His hand either.
10.31: The Jews picked up stones again tryna stone Him.
10.32: Jesus said, "I done showed y'all plenty of good works from My Father. Which one of 'em you stonin' Me for?"
10.33: They said, "It ain't 'cause of the good works—we stonin' You for blasphemy. You just a man, but You makin' Yourself God!"
10.34: Jesus said, "Y'all ever read in your law, 'I said y'all are gods'?
10.35: If Scripture called them gods—the ones who got God's word (and Scripture can't be broken)—
10.36: Then how y'all gon' say I'm blaspheming when the Father set Me apart and sent Me here, just 'cause I said I'm the Son of God?
10.37: If I ain't doin' My Father's works, then don't believe Me.
10.38: But if I am, even if y'all don't believe Me—at least believe the works, so y'all can know and understand the Father's in Me, and I'm in Him."
10.39: They tried to arrest Him again, but He slipped out they hands.
10.40: Jesus dipped back across the Jordan to the spot where John had first been baptizin'. He stayed out there.
10.41: A bunch of folks came out to Him and said, "John didn't do no miracles, but everything he said about this Man? It was true."
10.42: And a whole lotta them believed in Him out there.

11.1: There was a man named Lazarus who was real sick. He lived in Bethany, the same town Mary and her sister Martha was from.
11.2: This the same Mary who poured perfume on the Lord and wiped His feet with her hair—her brother Lazarus was the one sick.
11.3: So the sisters sent word to Jesus sayin', "Lord, the one You love is real sick."
11.4: When Jesus heard that, He said, "This sickness ain't gon' end in death—it's gon' show off God's glory and let the Son of God shine through it."
11.5: Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.
11.6: But even after He heard Lazarus was sick, He stayed right where He was for two more days.
11.7: After that, He told the disciples, "Alright, let's head back to Judea."
11.8: The disciples said, "Jesus, last time You was there they tried to stone You—and You tryna go back?"
11.9: Jesus said, "Ain't there twelve hours in the day? If you walk in the daytime, you ain't gon' stumble, 'cause you got light.
11.10: But if you walk at night, you gon' trip up, 'cause you can't see where you goin'."
11.11: Then He told 'em, "Our boy Lazarus sleepin', and I'm goin' to wake him up."
11.12: The disciples said, "Lord, if he sleepin', he'll get better."
11.13: But Jesus was talkin' about death—and they thought He meant like, nap nap.
11.14: So Jesus told 'em straight up, "Lazarus is dead.
11.15: And I'm glad I wasn't there—for y'all's sake—so y'all can really believe. Let's go see him."
11.16: Then Thomas (aka the Twin) said to the others, "Welp, let's go too—might as well die with Him."
11.17: When Jesus pulled up, He found out Lazarus had already been in the grave four whole days.
11.18: Bethany was just a couple miles from Jerusalem,
11.19: And a bunch of Jews had come through to comfort Martha and Mary 'bout their brother.
11.20: Soon as Martha heard Jesus was comin', she ran out to meet Him. Mary stayed in the house.
11.21: Martha said, "Lord, if You had been here, my brother wouldn't've died.
11.22: But even now, I know whatever You ask God, He gon' do it."
11.23: Jesus told her, "Your brother gon' rise again."
11.24: Martha said, "Yeah, I know he gon' rise at the resurrection, on the last day."
11.25: Jesus said, "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me, even if they die, they still gon' live.
11.26: And anybody who lives and believes in Me—ain't never really gon' die. You believe that?"
11.27: She said, "Yes, Lord—I believe You the Christ, the Son of God, the One we been waitin' on."
11.28: After she said that, she went and told Mary privately, "The Teacher here—He askin' for you."
11.29: Mary got up quick and went to Him.
11.30: Jesus hadn't made it to the house yet—He was still where Martha met Him.
11.31: The folks in the house saw Mary dip out fast, so they followed her, thinkin' she was headin' to the tomb to cry there.
11.32: When Mary saw Jesus, she dropped to His feet and said, "Lord, if You had been here, my brother wouldn't've died."
11.33: When Jesus saw her cryin', and all the folks cryin' too, He got mad in His spirit and was deeply bothered.
11.34: He asked, "Where y'all put him?" They said, "Lord, come see."
11.36: Then the people said, "Dang, He really loved him."
11.37: But some of them said, "Hold up—ain't this the same Man that opened blind eyes? Couldn't He have kept Lazarus from dyin'?"
11.38: Jesus, still lowkey mad, came to the tomb—it was a cave with a big ol' stone over the entrance.
11.39: Jesus said, "Roll the stone away." Martha said, "Lord, he been in there four days—he prolly stank by now."
11.40: Jesus said, "Didn't I tell you? If you believe, you gon' see God's glory."
11.41: So they moved the stone. Jesus looked up and said, "Father, thank You for hearin' Me.
11.42: I know You always hear Me, but I'm sayin' this out loud for all these folks standin' here—so they'll believe You sent Me."
11.43: Then He shouted, "Lazarus! Come on out!"
11.44: And Lazarus came walkin' out, still wrapped up in grave clothes and a cloth over his face. Jesus said, "Unwrap him. Let that man go."
11.45: A lot of the Jews who saw what Jesus did started believin' in Him.
11.46: But some of 'em ran back to the Pharisees and told on Him.
11.47: So the chief priests and Pharisees had a meeting. They said, "What we gon' do? This Man out here doin' all kinds of miracles.
11.48: If we let Him keep goin', everybody gon' believe in Him—and then Rome gon' come shut all this down and take everything."
11.49: Caiaphas, the high priest that year, said, "Y'all don't know what y'all talkin' 'bout.
11.50: Ain't it better for one man to die for the people, than for the whole nation to get wiped out?"
11.51: He ain't even realize he was prophesyin'—since he was high priest, he was speakin' what God had already planned: that Jesus would die for the nation.
11.52: And not just for them, but for all God's scattered children—to bring 'em together under one.
11.53: From that day on, they was seriously tryna kill Him.
11.54: So Jesus stopped movin' around publicly. He dipped out near the wilderness to a town called Ephraim and stayed there with the disciples.
11.55: The Passover was comin' up, and a lotta folks went to Jerusalem early to get themselves spiritually ready.
11.56: They kept lookin' for Jesus, whisperin' in the temple, "You think He gon' show up to the feast?"
11.57: The chief priests and Pharisees had already put out the word: "If anybody sees Him, let us know—so we can arrest Him."

12.1: Six days before Passover, Jesus pulled up in Bethany—that's where Lazarus stayed, the one Jesus brought back from the dead.
12.2: They threw a dinner for Him there. Martha was servin', and Lazarus was chillin' at the table with Jesus.
12.3: Then Mary came through with some expensive spikenard oil—like, real pricey. She anointed Jesus' feet and wiped 'em with her hair. Whole house was smellin' like that oil.
12.4: But Judas Iscariot—yeah, that one, the one who was gon' betray Him—said,
12.5: "Why didn't she sell that oil for like 300 denarii and give it to the poor?"
12.6: He ain't say that 'cause he cared 'bout the poor. Nah—he was a thief. He kept the money bag and used to help himself to it.
12.7: Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She savin' this moment for My burial.
12.8: Y'all always gon' have the poor with you, but y'all not always gon' have Me."
12.9: A bunch of Jews heard Jesus was in town, and they came through—not just for Him, but to see Lazarus too, the man He raised.
12.10: The chief priests started plottin' on Lazarus now too.
12.11: 'Cause of him, a whole lotta folks had started believin' in Jesus.
12.12: Next day, the crowd that came for the feast heard Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem.
12.13: They grabbed palm branches and ran out to meet Him, shoutin': "Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord—the King of Israel!"
12.14: Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, just like the Scriptures said:
12.15: "Don't trip, daughter of Zion. Your King comin'—riding on a young donkey."
12.16: His disciples ain't catch the meaning of all this at first. But after Jesus got glorified, they looked back and was like, "Ohhh that's what that was about!"
12.17: The folks who were there when Jesus raised Lazarus from the grave—they was tellin' everybody what they saw.
12.18: That's why the crowd came out—they heard about that miracle.
12.19: The Pharisees was heated. They said, "Look, we ain't gettin' nowhere. The whole world chasin' after Him now."
12.20: Some Greeks came to worship during the feast.
12.21: They found Philip (he from Bethsaida) and said, "Sir, we tryna see Jesus."
12.22: Philip told Andrew, and together they went and told Jesus.
12.23: Jesus said, "It's time. The Son of Man 'bout to be glorified.
12.24: Listen up—unless a grain of wheat falls in the dirt and dies, it stays solo. But if it dies? It multiplies.
12.25: If you too in love with your life, you gon' lose it. But if you willing to let it go for Me, you gon' gain eternal life.
12.26: If you serve Me, follow Me. Wherever I'm at, that's where My servant should be. And if you serve Me, My Father gon' honor you."
12.27: "Man… My soul is feelin' real heavy. But what I'ma say? 'Father, save Me from this?' Nah—this the whole reason I came.
12.28: Father, glorify Your name." Then a voice came from heaven: "I done glorified it, and I'ma glorify it again."
12.29: The crowd that heard it was like, "Did it just thunder?" Others said, "Nah, that was an angel talkin' to Him."
12.30: Jesus said, "That voice wasn't for Me—it was for y'all.
12.31: The time done come for the world to get judged. The devil—yeah, the ruler of this world—'bout to get kicked out.
12.32: And when I get lifted up from the earth, I'm drawin' everybody to Myself."
12.33: (He said this to let them know how He was gon' die.)
12.34: The people said, "Hold up—we thought the Messiah supposed to live forever. What you mean 'lifted up'? Who is this Son of Man?"
12.35: Jesus said, "Y'all got the light just a little while longer. Walk in the light now, before darkness catch you slippin'. If you walk in the dark, you don't know where you goin'.
12.36: While you got the light, believe in the light, so y'all can become children of light." After He said that, Jesus dipped off and hid from them.
12.37: Even with all the miracles Jesus did, they still didn't believe.
12.38: Just like Isaiah said: "Lord, who believed our message? Who saw the Lord's power revealed?"
12.39: And they couldn't believe—'cause Isaiah also said:
12.40: "He blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, So they wouldn't see, Wouldn't understand, Wouldn't turn to Me, And get healed."
12.41: Isaiah said that 'cause he saw Jesus' glory and spoke 'bout Him.
12.42: Even some of the leaders believed—but they kept it low. They ain't confess it, 'cause they ain't wanna get kicked out the synagogue.
12.43: They cared more 'bout what folks thought than what God thought.
12.44: Jesus cried out, "If you believe in Me, you really believe in the One who sent Me.
12.45: When you look at Me, you see the One who sent Me.
12.46: I came into the world as light, so whoever believes in Me don't gotta stay in the dark.
12.47: If somebody hears Me and don't believe, I ain't here to judge 'em—I came to save the world.
12.48: But if you reject Me and don't take in My words, the word itself gon' judge you on the last day.
12.49: I ain't speakin' on My own—I'm sayin' what the Father told Me to say.
12.50: And I know His command leads to eternal life. So whatever I say—it's exactly what He told Me to say."

13.1: Right before Passover, Jesus knew His time was almost up. He was 'bout to leave this world and go back to the Father. He had mad love for His people, and He ain't stop lovin' them—not even at the end.
13.2: They had just finished eatin'. The devil had already dropped that idea into Judas' heart—to betray Jesus.
13.3: Jesus knew the Father put everything in His hands. He knew He came from God and was goin' back to God.
13.4: So He got up from dinner, took off His outer clothes, grabbed a towel, and wrapped it around Himself.
13.5: Then He poured water in a bowl and started washin' His disciples' feet—wipin' 'em with the towel He was wearin'.
13.6: He got to Simon Peter. Peter said, "Lord, You really finna wash my feet?"
13.7: Jesus said, "You don't get it now, but you will later."
13.8: Peter said, "Nah, You ain't never washin' my feet." Jesus said, "If I don't wash you, then you not rockin' with Me. No part of this."
13.9: Peter was like, "Well in that case, Lord, go 'head and wash my hands and head too!"
13.10: Jesus told him, "If you already had a bath, you just need your feet done. You already clean—but not all of y'all."
13.11: He knew who was gon' betray Him. That's why He said, "Not all y'all clean."
13.12: After He washed their feet, He got dressed again and sat down. He said, "Y'all know what I just did for y'all?"
13.13: "You call Me 'Teacher' and 'Lord,' and you right—I am that.
13.14: So if I, your Lord and Teacher, washed your feet, y'all should wash each other's feet too.
13.15: I gave y'all a whole example—do like I did.
13.16: Listen close: ain't no servant greater than the one who sent 'em. Ain't no messenger above the one who sent the message.
13.17: If you know this, you blessed if you do it."
13.18: "Now look—I ain't talkin' 'bout everybody. I know who I chose. But Scripture gotta play out: 'The one who ate bread with Me done turned on Me.'
13.19: I'm tellin' y'all now before it happen, so when it does, y'all know I am who I said I am.
13.20: Truth is, whoever welcomes the one I send, welcomes Me. And if you welcome Me, you welcoming the One who sent Me."
13.21: After that, Jesus got real heavy in His spirit. He said, "I'm tellin' y'all the truth—one of y'all 'bout to betray Me."
13.22: The disciples started lookin' at each other, confused, tryin' to figure out who He talkin' 'bout.
13.23: One of the disciples—Jesus really loved him—was leanin' on Jesus' chest.
13.24: Simon Peter motioned to him, like, "Ask Him who He talkin' 'bout."
13.25: So that disciple leaned in and said, "Lord, who is it?"
13.26: Jesus said, "The one I'm gon' give this dipped piece of bread to." Then He dipped the bread and handed it to Judas Iscariot.
13.27: Soon as Judas took the bread, Satan entered him. Jesus said, "What you 'bout to do, go do it quick."
13.28: Nobody else at the table had a clue what Jesus meant by that.
13.29: Some thought, since Judas kept the money bag, Jesus was tellin' him to go buy stuff for the feast or give to the poor.
13.30: Soon as Judas took the bread, he bounced. And it was night.
13.31: After Judas left, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God gettin' His glory through Him.
13.32: If God's gettin' glory through Him, then God gon' glorify Him too—and He ain't waitin' to do it."
13.33: "Lil' children, I'ma be with y'all just a lil' longer. You gon' look for Me, but like I told the Jews, 'Where I'm goin', you can't come.' Same goes for y'all right now.
13.34: I'm givin' y'all a new commandment—love each other. Just like I loved y'all, that's how you should love one another.
13.35: That's how everybody gon' know you My people—if you got love for each other."
13.36: Simon Peter asked, "Lord, where You goin'?" Jesus said, "Where I'm headed, you can't come now—but you'll follow later."
13.37: Peter said, "Why not now, Lord? I'll die for You!"
13.38: Jesus said, "Oh you would? For real? I'm tellin' you straight up—the rooster ain't even gon' crow before you deny Me three times."

14.1: Don't let your heart be heavy. You believe in God? Cool. Believe in Me too.
14.2: In My Father's house, there's plenty rooms—more than enough for everybody. If it wasn't like that, I woulda told y'all. I'm goin' ahead to get the spot ready for you.
14.3: And if I go get things set up, best believe I'ma come back and scoop y'all up, so we can be together.
14.4: Y'all already know where I'm headed—and you know the way there too.
14.5: Thomas said, "Lord, we don't even know where You goin'. How we supposed to know the way?"
14.6: Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life. Ain't nobody gettin' to the Father unless they come through Me."
14.7: "If y'all really knew Me, you'd know My Father too. From now on, y'all know Him—and you done seen Him."
14.8: Philip said, "Lord, just show us the Father. That'll be enough."
14.9: Jesus said, "Forreal, Philip? I been here with y'all all this time, and you still don't know Me? If you seen Me, you seen the Father. So why you askin' Me to show Him to you?"
14.10: "Don't you believe I'm in the Father, and the Father in Me? The words I speak ain't just from Me—they from the Father, doin' His thing through Me."
14.11: "Believe Me when I say I'm in the Father and He in Me. Or at least believe 'cause of the works you seen."
14.12: "I'm tellin' y'all the truth: whoever believes in Me will do the stuff I been doin'—and even greater—'cause I'm goin' to the Father."
14.13: "And whatever you ask in My name, I'ma do it, so the Father can get the glory through the Son."
14.14: "If y'all ask anything in My name, I'ma handle it."
14.15: "If you love Me, show it by doin' what I say."
14.16: "And I'ma ask the Father to send y'all another Helper, somebody who gon' stick with you forever."
14.17: "That's the Spirit of truth. The world can't receive Him—they can't see Him or recognize Him. But you know Him, 'cause He stay with y'all, and soon He'll be in you."
14.18: "I'm not leavin' y'all hangin'. I'ma come back for you."
14.19: "In a minute, the world won't see Me no more. But y'all gon' see Me. Because I'm alive, y'all gon' live too."
14.20: "That day, y'all gon' realize—I'm in the Father, y'all in Me, and I'm in y'all."
14.21: "The one who knows My commands and lives by 'em? That's the one who really love Me. And My Father gon' love them, and I'ma love them too—and show up in their life, clear as day."
14.22: Judas (not Iscariot) asked, "Lord, how You gon' show up to us, but not to the world?"
14.23: Jesus said, "If anybody love Me, they gon' keep My word. And My Father gon' love 'em too. We gon' pull up and make ourselves at home in their heart."
14.24: "But the one who don't love Me? They ain't tryna hear My words. And what I'm sayin' ain't just from Me—it's from the Father who sent Me."
14.25: "I been tellin' y'all all this while I'm still here with you."
14.26: "But the Helper—the Holy Spirit—the Father gon' send Him in My name. He gon' teach you everything and help you remember all I done told y'all."
14.27: "I'm leavin' you peace. My peace—not like the world give. Don't let your heart be troubled or scared."
14.28: "Y'all heard Me say, 'I'm leavin' but I'ma come back.' If you really loved Me, you'd be happy for Me, 'cause I'm goin' to the Father—and He greater than Me."
14.29: "I'm tellin' y'all now, before it happen, so when it does, y'all'll believe."
14.30: "I ain't got much more time to talk. The enemy—the ruler of this world—is comin'. But he ain't got nothin' on Me."
14.31: "I'ma do what the Father told Me, so the world knows I love Him. Now come on—let's go."

15.1: "I'm the real vine, and My Father the one takin' care of the garden."
15.2: "Every branch on Me that ain't producin' nothin'? He snip it off. And the ones that do bear fruit? He still trimmin' 'em—so they can grow even more."
15.3: "Y'all already clean 'cause of the word I done spoke over you."
15.4: "Stay connected to Me, and I'ma stay connected to you. A branch can't do nothin' on its own—it gotta stay on the vine. Same with y'all—you can't bear no fruit unless you stay in Me."
15.5: "I'm the vine, y'all the branches. If you stay in Me, and I'm in you, you gon' bear mad fruit. But without Me? You can't do nothin'."
15.6: "Anybody who don't stay in Me is like a dry branch—cut off, tossed out, and burned up."
15.7: "But if you stay rooted in Me, and My words stay in you, go 'head and ask for what you want—it'll be done."
15.8: "When you bear a lotta fruit, that's when My Father get the glory—and that's how folks know y'all My disciples."
15.9: "Just like the Father love Me, I love y'all too. Stay right there in My love."
15.10: "Keep My commandments, and you'll stay in My love—just like I kept My Father's and stayed in His."
15.11: "I told y'all all this so My joy can be in you—and so your joy can be full to the brim."
15.12: "Here's My command: love each other the way I loved y'all."
15.13: "Ain't no love bigger than this—somebody layin' down they life for they friends."
15.14: "Y'all My friends if you do what I say."
15.15: "I don't call y'all servants no more. A servant don't know what the boss doin'. But I call y'all friends, 'cause I told y'all everything My Father told Me."
15.16: "Y'all ain't choose Me—I chose you. I picked y'all and set you up to go out here and bear fruit. Fruit that lasts. And whatever you ask the Father in My name? He got you."
15.17: "This what I'm tellin' y'all again—love each other."
15.18: "If the world hatin' on you, just know they hated Me first."
15.19: "If you belonged to the world, it'd love you like one of its own. But nah—I chose you out the world. That's why they hatin'."
15.20: "Remember what I told y'all: a servant ain't greater than the master. They came for Me? They gon' come for y'all too. If they kept My word, some'll keep yours too."
15.21: "They gon' do all this mess to y'all 'cause of My name—'cause they don't even know the One who sent Me."
15.22: "If I ain't come and told 'em the truth, they'd have an excuse. But now? They know better."
15.23: "If they hate Me, they hatin' My Father too."
15.24: "I did things nobody else ever done. They seen it. They know—but they still hate Me and My Father."
15.25: "But all this went down so Scripture would come true: 'They hated Me without no reason.'"
15.26: "But when the Helper come—the one I'ma send y'all from the Father, the Spirit of truth—He gon' speak up for Me."
15.27: "And y'all gon' bear witness too—'cause y'all been rockin' with Me since day one."

16.1: "I'm tellin' y'all all this so you don't trip or fall off."
16.2: "They gon' kick you out the synagogues, no lie. And it's gon' get so wild that folks who killin' y'all gon' really think they doin' God a favor."
16.3: "They doin' all this 'cause they don't know Me or the Father. Straight up."
16.4: "But I'm lettin' y'all know ahead of time—so when it pop off, you remember I said it. I ain't say nothin' earlier 'cause I was still here with you."
16.5: "But now I'm headin' back to the One who sent Me—and not one of y'all askin' Me, 'Where You goin'?'"
16.6: "Y'all just heartbroken after what I said. I feel that."
16.7: "But let Me keep it real: it's actually better for y'all that I dip. 'Cause if I don't go, the Helper won't come through. But if I leave? I'ma send Him right to you."
16.8: "And when He show up, He gon' call the world out—on sin, on righteousness, and on judgment."
16.9: "On sin? 'Cause they don't believe in Me."
16.10: "On righteousness? 'Cause I'm goin' to the Father, and y'all won't see Me no more."
16.11: "On judgment? 'Cause the enemy—the ruler of this world—already caught that L."
16.12: "I got so much more to tell y'all, but y'all ain't ready yet."
16.13: "But when the Spirit of truth pull up, He gon' guide you into all truth. He ain't speakin' on His own either—He only sayin' what He hear. And He gon' let y'all know what's comin'."
16.14: "He gon' shine the light on Me—'cause He gon' take what's Mine and hand it to y'all."
16.15: "Everything the Father got? That's Mine. That's why I said He takin' what's Mine and makin' it known to y'all."
16.16: "In a lil' bit, you ain't gon' see Me no more. But then, not too long after, you will see Me again. 'Cause I'm goin' to the Father."
16.17: So the disciples start whisperin' like, "What He mean 'a lil' while'? And why He say 'goin' to the Father' like that?"
16.18: "We don't get it, man. What's He talkin' about?"
16.19: Jesus peeped their confusion and said, "Y'all wonderin' what I meant by 'a lil' while'? Lemme break it down."
16.20: "Y'all gon' cry and mourn while the world celebratin'. But don't trip—your sorrow gon' flip into joy."
16.21: "It's like a woman in labor—she hurtin' bad, but soon as that baby drop? She don't even think about the pain no more 'cause of the joy."
16.22: "That's y'all right now—sad. But I'ma see you again, and your heart gon' light up. And can't nobody snatch that joy away from you."
16.23: "On that day, you ain't even gotta ask Me nothin'. Whatever y'all ask the Father in My name? He gon' do it."
16.24: "Up 'til now, y'all ain't asked nothin' in My name. Start askin'—so y'all can receive, and your joy be on full."
16.25: "I been speakin' in parables, but soon I'ma keep it all the way plain with y'all about the Father."
16.26: "And in that day, y'all gon' pray in My name. I ain't sayin' I gotta beg the Father for you—"
16.27: "'Cause the Father Himself love y'all. Why? 'Cause y'all loved Me and believed I came from Him."
16.28: "I came from the Father into this world. Now I'm bout to leave the world and go back to Him."
16.29: The disciples were like, "Okay! Now You talkin' plain—no more riddles."
16.30: "We get it now. You know everything. You ain't gotta wait on nobody to ask questions. That's why we believe You came from God."
16.31: Jesus was like, "Y'all believe now, huh?"
16.32: "Well, check this—the time comin' (matter fact, it's here now) when y'all gon' scatter. Everybody goin' they own way, leavin' Me solo. But I ain't alone—My Father with Me."
16.33: "I told y'all all this so you can have peace in Me. Out here in the world, it's gon' be rough. But keep your head up—I done beat the world already."

17.1: Jesus looked up to heaven and said, "Aight, Father, the time here now. Go 'head and shine on Your Son, so I can shine right back on You."
17.2: "You done gave Me the power over everybody, and I'ma use it to bless the ones You gave Me—with eternal life."
17.3: "And real eternal life? It's knowin' You, the one true God, and knowin' Me, Jesus the Christ, who You sent."
17.4: "I held it down for You on earth. I finished what You gave Me to do."
17.5: "So now, Father, bring Me back into that same glory I had with You before the world even existed."
17.6: "I made Your name known to the ones You pulled out the world and gave to Me. They was Yours, and You passed them to Me, and they been holdin' on to Your word."
17.7: "Now they know for sure everything You gave Me came straight from You."
17.8: "I gave 'em the words You gave Me, and they received it. They believe I came from You. They locked in."
17.9: "I'm prayin' for them—not for the world, but for them, the ones You gave Me. They Yours."
17.10: "Everything I got is Yours, and everything You got is Mine. And they makin' Me look good out here."
17.11: "I'm bout to bounce from the world, but they still gon' be here. Father, hold 'em down in Your name—the name You gave Me—so they can be one, just like Us."
17.12: "When I was with 'em, I kept 'em safe in Your name. Ain't none of 'em got lost—except for that one, the son of destruction—so Scripture could be fulfilled."
17.13: "But now I'm comin' back to You. I'm sayin' this out loud while I'm still here so they can have My joy deep in they hearts."
17.14: "I gave 'em Your word, and the world hated 'em for it—'cause they not of this world, just like I ain't."
17.15: "I ain't askin' You to take 'em out the world. Just keep 'em safe from the evil one."
17.16: "They not of this world, same way I ain't of it."
17.17: "Make 'em holy through the truth. Your word is truth."
17.18: "Just like You sent Me into the world, I'm sendin' them too."
17.19: "And I'm settin' Myself apart for them, so they can be made holy too, through the truth."
17.20: "I ain't just prayin' for them right now—I'm also prayin' for everybody who gon' believe in Me through what they say."
17.21: "I want all of 'em to be one, just like You and Me are one—Me in You, You in Me. So they can be one with Us, and the world finally believe You sent Me."
17.22: "The same glory You gave Me? I gave it to them—so they can be one, just like Us."
17.23: "I'm in them, You in Me—so they can be made complete as one. Then the world gon' know You sent Me, and that You love them like You love Me."
17.24: "Father, I want them ones You gave Me to be with Me where I'm at. I want them to see My glory—the glory You gave Me 'cause You loved Me before the world even started."
17.25: "Righteous Father, the world don't know You, but I do. And these ones here? They know You sent Me."
17.26: "I let 'em know who You are—and I'ma keep doin' it—so the same love You got for Me can live in them. And I'ma be in them too."

18.1: After Jesus finished prayin', He dipped out wit' His disciples, crossed the Kidron brook, and went into a garden spot He used to chill at with them.
18.2: Judas—yeah, the one who snitched—knew 'bout that spot too, 'cause Jesus had been meetin' there with His people.
18.3: So Judas pulled up, rollin' deep with soldiers and Temple guards from the chief priests and Pharisees. They came through strapped—lanterns, torches, weapons and all.
18.4: Jesus, knowin' exactly what was about to pop off, stepped forward and asked, "Who y'all lookin' for?"
18.5: They said, "Jesus from Nazareth." Jesus said, "That's Me." Judas—the backstabber—was right there wit' them.
18.6: When Jesus said, "That's Me," they fell back and hit the ground.
18.7: So He asked again, "Who y'all lookin' for?" They said, "Jesus from Nazareth."
18.8: Jesus said, "I done told y'all already—it's Me. So if I'm who you want, let My people go."
18.9: That way, what He had said before would come true: "I ain't lost none of the ones You gave Me."
18.10: Then Simon Peter pulled out a sword and sliced off the right ear of the high priest's servant. That dude's name was Malchus.
18.11: Jesus told Peter, "Put that sword up. You think I ain't gon' take this cup My Father gave Me?"
18.12: Then the crew—the soldiers, their leader, and the Jewish officials—grabbed Jesus, tied Him up,
18.13: and dragged Him to Annas first. He was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
18.14: Caiaphas the one who told the Jews, "It's better if one man dies for everybody."
18.15: Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple. That one had some clout—he knew the high priest—so he got into the courtyard with Jesus.
18.16: Peter was still outside. The other disciple talked to the girl at the door and got Peter in.
18.17: The girl said, "You not one of His people too, are you?" Peter said, "Nah, I'm not."
18.18: It was cold, so the servants and guards had a fire going. Peter was there too, tryin' to warm up with them.
18.19: Then the high priest started grillin' Jesus about His disciples and His message.
18.20: Jesus said, "I been speakin' out in the open—synagogues, Temple, you name it. I ain't keep nothin' on the low."
18.21: "Why you askin' Me? Ask the folks who heard Me—they know what I said."
18.22: One of the guards slapped Jesus and said, "That how you talk to the high priest?"
18.23: Jesus said, "If I said somethin' wrong, say what it was. But if I didn't, why you hit Me?"
18.24: Then Annas sent Jesus—still tied up—to Caiaphas the high priest.
18.25: Meanwhile, Peter was still outside tryin' to keep warm. They said to him, "You ain't one of His people too, are you?" He said, "I'm not."
18.26: Then one of the high priest's servants—kin to the dude Peter cut—said, "Didn't I see you in the garden with Him?"
18.27: Peter denied it again. And right then, a rooster crowed.
18.28: They took Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor's HQ—it was still early. The Jews didn't go inside 'cause they didn't wanna mess up their Passover rituals.
18.29: So Pilate came outside and said, "What y'all accusin' this Man of?"
18.30: They said, "If He wasn't doin' wrong, we wouldn't've brought Him to you."
18.31: Pilate said, "Y'all handle it by your own law." They said, "We can't execute nobody."
18.32: That was so Jesus' own words about how He'd die would come true.
18.33: Pilate went back inside, called Jesus in, and said, "You the King of the Jews?"
18.34: Jesus said, "You askin' that for yourself, or did somebody put that in your ear?"
18.35: Pilate said, "Bruh, I ain't Jewish. Your people and your religious leaders handed you over. What you do?"
18.36: Jesus said, "My kingdom ain't from here. If it was, My people would've been throwin' hands to keep Me from gettin' arrested. But nah, that ain't what this is."
