18.37: Pilate said, "So you a king then?" Jesus said, "You said it. I came here to speak truth. Everybody who's bout that truth hears Me."
18.38: Pilate said, "What even is truth?" Then he walked back out and told the Jews, "I don't see no reason to charge this dude.
18.39: But it's y'all's custom for me to let somebody go at Passover. You want me to let the 'King of the Jews' go?"
18.40: They yelled, "Nah, not Him! Give us Barabbas!" Barabbas was a straight-up robber.

19.1: Then Pilate had Jesus whipped—straight up scourged Him.
19.2: The soldiers twisted up a crown made of thorns and jammed it on His head. Then they threw a purple robe on Him.
19.3: They kept mockin' Him like, "Hail, King of the Jews!" And they smacked Him up too.
19.4: Pilate came back out and said, "Look, I'm bringin' Him out to y'all to show I don't see nothin' wrong with Him."
19.5: Then Jesus stepped out, wearin' the crown of thorns and that purple robe. Pilate said, "Behold the Man!"
19.6: When the chief priests and guards saw Him, they yelled, "Crucify Him! Crucify Him!" Pilate said, "Y'all do it. I ain't find no fault in Him."
19.7: The Jews replied, "We got a law, and by that law He gotta die, 'cause He said He God's Son."
19.8: When Pilate heard that, he got even more shook.
19.9: He went back inside and asked Jesus, "Where you really from?" But Jesus didn't say nothin'.
19.10: Pilate said, "You not gon' talk to me? Don't you know I got power to crucify you or let you go?"
19.11: Jesus said, "You wouldn't have no power over Me unless it was given from above. The one who handed Me over got the bigger sin."
19.12: From then on Pilate tried to let Him go, but the Jews shouted, "If you let Him go, you not down with Caesar. Anybody callin' themself a king is goin' against Caesar!"
19.13: When Pilate heard that, he brought Jesus out and sat on the judge's seat at a place called The Pavement—Gabbatha in Hebrew.
19.14: It was the day before Passover, around noon. Pilate said, "Behold your King!"
19.15: But they shouted back, "Get Him outta here! Crucify Him!" Pilate asked, "Should I crucify y'all's King?" The chief priests said, "We ain't got no king but Caesar!"
19.16: So Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified. They took Jesus and led Him away.
19.17: Jesus carried His own cross to a place called The Skull—Golgotha in Hebrew.
19.18: That's where they crucified Him, with two others—one on each side and Jesus in the middle.
19.19: Pilate had a sign made and nailed it on the cross. It read: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
19.20: A lotta folks read that sign, since the spot was close to the city. It was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.
19.21: Then the chief priests told Pilate, "Don't write 'The King of the Jews.' Say, 'He said He was King of the Jews.'"
19.22: Pilate said, "What I wrote is what I wrote."
19.23: When the soldiers crucified Jesus, they took His clothes and split 'em four ways, one part for each soldier. The tunic was seamless, woven all in one piece.
19.24: They said, "Let's not rip it—let's roll dice for it." That fulfilled what Scripture said: 'They divided My clothes and threw lots for My robe.' So that's what they did.
19.25: Jesus' mama was standin' by the cross, along with her sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
19.26: Jesus saw His mama there, and the disciple He loved nearby. He said to His mama, "Woman, here's your son."
19.27: Then He said to the disciple, "Here's your mama." From then on, that disciple took her into his home.
19.28: After that, knowin' everything was now done to fulfill the Scriptures, Jesus said, "I'm thirsty."
19.29: There was a jar of sour wine there, so they soaked a sponge in it, stuck it on some hyssop, and put it to His mouth.
19.30: When Jesus took the wine, He said, "It's finished." Then He bowed His head and let go of His spirit.
19.31: Since it was Preparation Day and they didn't want the bodies up there during the Sabbath (and this one was a big deal), the Jews asked Pilate to break their legs and take the bodies down.
19.32: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man and then the other who was crucified next to Jesus.
19.33: But when they got to Jesus and saw He was already dead, they didn't break His legs.
19.34: Instead, one of the soldiers stabbed His side with a spear—and out came blood and water.
19.35: The one who saw it gave his testimony, and it's real. He tellin' the truth so y'all can believe.
19.36: All this happened to fulfill Scripture: 'Not one of His bones will be broken.'
19.37: Another verse says: 'They'll look at the One they pierced.'
19.38: Later, Joseph from Arimathea—who followed Jesus on the low 'cause he was scared of the Jews—asked Pilate if he could take Jesus' body. Pilate said yes, so he took it.
19.39: Nicodemus came too—yeah, the one who visited Jesus at night—bringin' about 100 pounds of myrrh and aloes.
19.40: They wrapped Jesus' body with the spices in linen strips—just like the Jewish burial customs.
19.41: The place where He was crucified had a garden, and in that garden was a new tomb nobody had used yet.
19.42: So they laid Jesus there, since it was the Jewish Prep Day and the tomb was close by.

20.1: Early Sunday mornin', while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene pulled up to the tomb and saw that the stone had been rolled away.
20.2: She ran straight to Simon Peter and the other disciple Jesus loved and said, "They done took the Lord out the tomb, and we don't know where they put Him!"
20.3: So Peter and the other disciple took off, headed for the tomb.
20.4: They ran together, but the other disciple outran Peter and got there first.
20.5: He leaned down and peeked in—saw the linen cloths sittin' there—but he ain't go inside.
20.6: Then Simon Peter caught up, went straight into the tomb, and saw the linen cloths too.
20.7: He also saw the cloth that had been on Jesus' head. It wasn't with the other linen but folded up nice and neat in a separate spot.
20.8: Then the other disciple, the one who got there first, finally stepped in. He saw—and he believed.
20.9: They still ain't fully understand the Scripture yet, that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
20.10: So the disciples went back to they homes.
20.11: But Mary stayed posted outside the tomb, cryin'. As she wept, she leaned down and looked inside.
20.12: She saw two angels in white, one sittin' at the head and one at the foot where Jesus' body had been.
20.13: They asked her, "Ma'am, why you cryin'?" She said, "They took my Lord, and I don't know where they put Him."
20.14: Right after she said that, she turned around and saw Jesus standin' there—but she ain't realize it was Him.
20.15: Jesus said, "Why you cryin'? Who you lookin' for?" She thought He was the gardener and said, "Sir, if you moved Him, just tell me where and I'll go get Him."
20.16: Jesus said, "Mary." She turned and said, "Rabboni!" (That means Teacher.)
20.17: Jesus told her, "Don't hold on to Me, 'cause I haven't gone up to the Father yet. But go tell My brothers: 'I'm goin' up to My Father and y'all's Father, My God and y'all's God.'"
20.18: Mary Magdalene ran back and told the disciples, "I seen the Lord!" and she told 'em everything He said.
20.19: That evening, on the first day of the week, the disciples were hid behind locked doors 'cause they was scared of the Jews. Jesus just pulled up in the middle of 'em and said, "Peace y'all."
20.20: Then He showed them His hands and His side. When they saw it was really the Lord, they got hype.
20.21: Jesus said again, "Peace, fam. Just like the Father sent Me, I'm sendin' y'all."
20.22: Then He breathed on them and said, "Catch this: Receive the Holy Spirit.
20.23: If y'all forgive somebody's sins, they forgiven. But if y'all hold on to it, it's held."
20.24: Now Thomas (aka the Twin), one of the twelve, wasn't there when Jesus showed up.
20.25: So the rest told him, "Yo, we seen the Lord!" But Thomas said, "Unless I see the nail prints in His hands and touch 'em, and put my hand in His side—I ain't buyin' it."
20.26: Eight days later, the disciples were together again—Thomas with them this time. Even though the doors was locked, Jesus came through and stood right there. He said, "Peace, fam."
20.27: Then He told Thomas, "Go head—touch My hands. Reach here and feel My side. Stop doubting and believe."
20.28: Thomas said, "My Lord and my God!"
20.29: Jesus said, "You believe 'cause you seen Me? Blessed are the ones who ain't seen Me but still believe."
20.30: Jesus did way more signs in front of the disciples than what's in this book.
20.31: But these right here was written so y'all can believe that Jesus is the Christ, God's Son—and by believin', you'll have life in His name.

21.1: After all that, Jesus popped up again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias, and here's how it went down:
21.2: Simon Peter, Thomas (the one they call the Twin), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the Zebedee brothers, and two other disciples were all chillin' together.
21.3: Simon Peter said, "I'm goin' fishin'." They said, "Bet, we rollin' too." So they hit the boat, but all night long—they ain't catch a thing.
21.4: Come sunrise, Jesus was standin' on the shore, but the crew ain't realize it was Him.
21.5: Jesus called out, "Y'all got anything to eat?" They said, "Nah."
21.6: He said, "Throw the net on the right side of the boat—you'll find some." So they did, and boom—the net was heavy with fish, too many to pull in.
21.7: Then the disciple Jesus loved said to Peter, "Yo—it's the Lord!" When Peter heard that, he threw on his outer robe and jumped into the water like he ain't care 'bout nothin' else.
21.8: The rest of the crew came in the small boat, draggin' that net full of fish. They was only like a football field away from shore.
21.9: When they got to land, they saw a charcoal fire burnin', with fish cookin' and some bread layin' out.
21.10: Jesus said, "Go on and bring some of them fish y'all just caught."
21.11: Simon Peter dragged that net up on shore, full of big fish—153 to be exact. And even with all that, the net ain't rip.
21.12: Jesus said, "Come eat breakfast." Ain't nobody dared ask, "Who are You?" 'cause deep down, they knew it was the Lord.
21.13: Jesus came through, took the bread, and passed it out—did the same with the fish.
21.14: That was the third time Jesus showed up to the disciples after He came back from the dead.
21.15: After breakfast, Jesus asked Simon Peter, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love Me more than these?" Peter said, "Yeah, Lord. You know I love You." Jesus said, "Then feed My lambs."
21.16: Jesus asked again, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love Me?" Peter said, "Yes, Lord, You know I love You." Jesus said, "Take care of My sheep."
21.17: A third time, Jesus asked, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love Me?" That hit Peter hard. He was hurt Jesus asked a third time. He said, "Lord, You know everything. You know I love You." Jesus said, "Feed My sheep.
21.18: For real, for real—I'm tellin' you: when you was young, you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted. But when you get old, you gon' stretch out your hands, and somebody else gon' dress you and take you somewhere you don't wanna go."
21.19: Jesus said that to hint at what kind of death Peter would die to honor God. Then He told him, "Follow Me."
21.20: Peter turned around and saw the disciple Jesus loved followin'—the same one who leaned back on Jesus during dinner and asked, "Lord, who's gon' betray You?"
21.21: Peter looked at that disciple and said, "Lord, what about him?"
21.22: Jesus said, "If I want him to stick around till I come back, what's that got to do with you? You—follow Me."
21.23: So the word started spreadin' that this disciple wouldn't die. But Jesus ain't say that—He just said, "If I want him to stay till I return, what's that to you?"
21.24: This the disciple who's tellin' y'all all this, and who wrote it down. And we know his word solid.
21.25: Jesus did so much more too—if they wrote it all down, shoot, I don't think the whole world could hold all the books.
